questions.question: Which statement best characterizes bag-of-words and shallow embedding classifiers as used in fastText-style systems?
questions.choice_A: They model long-range word dependencies by building deep recurrent networks over token sequences.
questions.choice_B: They represent documents as sums or averages of learned word (and n-gram) embeddings, enabling fast linear classification.
questions.choice_C: They require sentence-level parse trees to construct document vectors for classification.
questions.choice_D: They rely primarily on topic models like LDA to produce input features for a deep classifier.

questions.question: What is the core architectural idea behind fastText for supervised classification?
questions.choice_A: A linear classifier operating on the averaged embeddings of words and n-grams, optionally with subword features
questions.choice_B: A transformer encoder with multi-head attention over word pieces
questions.choice_C: A convolutional neural network that scans over character trigrams
questions.choice_D: A hierarchical recurrent network with attention and CRF decoding

questions.question: Why are n-gram features useful in fastText-style classifiers for web page filtering?
questions.choice_A: They eliminate the need for any tokenization at training time.
questions.choice_B: They force the model to learn syntactic trees explicitly.
questions.choice_C: They partially capture local word order and common phrases, improving discrimination over pure unigrams.
questions.choice_D: They guarantee perfect generalization to unseen domains without additional data.

questions.question: Which of the following is least relevant as a fastText training hyperparameter for controlling accuracy/speed trade-offs in text classification?
questions.choice_A: Embedding dimension and number of epochs
questions.choice_B: Learning rate and choice of loss (softmax, hs, ns, ova)
questions.choice_C: Word and character n-gram settings (e.g., wordNgrams, minn/maxn) and bucket size
questions.choice_D: Batch normalization momentum and dropout rate schedules

questions.question: When using a classifier for retrieval, under what circumstance would you generally raise the decision threshold?
questions.choice_A: When you want to recover more positives at the cost of including more false positives
questions.choice_B: When you require higher precision and can tolerate missing some relevant items
questions.choice_C: When class imbalance is severe and positives are very rare, regardless of precision needs
questions.choice_D: When optimizing for recall at fixed precision

questions.question: Which practice best leverages positive and negative seeds to improve a domain filter over time?
questions.choice_A: Using only easy negatives with obviously unrelated pages to avoid confusing the model
questions.choice_B: Discarding negative examples once validation accuracy surpasses 95%
questions.choice_C: Balancing the training set by duplicating positive seeds until classes are equal without adding new data
questions.choice_D: Continuously mining near-miss negatives that score highly but are not relevant, and incorporating them into training

questions.question: Which description best matches iterative hard-negative mining in classifier-based retrieval?
questions.choice_A: Score a large unlabeled pool, collect high-scoring false positives, add them as negatives, retrain, and repeat
questions.choice_B: Randomly sample negatives each epoch to avoid overfitting to any specific negative set
questions.choice_C: Use only positives for training and rely on thresholding to handle negatives
questions.choice_D: Train once on initial seeds and deploy without updating to preserve calibration

questions.question: When scaling fastText-style classification to billions of web pages, why is feature hashing (e.g., buckets for n-grams) important?
questions.choice_A: It increases precision by removing ambiguous tokens from the vocabulary.
questions.choice_B: It ensures exact preservation of all n-gram identities without collisions.
questions.choice_C: It bounds the memory footprint of the feature space by mapping many n-grams into a fixed-size index range.
questions.choice_D: It eliminates the need for distributed processing during inference.

questions.question: For highly imbalanced web-scale retrieval (positives are rare), which evaluation is generally most informative for threshold selection?
questions.choice_A: Overall accuracy on the full unlabeled web crawl
questions.choice_B: Precision-recall curve and average precision on a labeled evaluation set
questions.choice_C: Confusion matrix computed with a 50/50 positive/negative test set
questions.choice_D: Mean squared error of predicted probabilities

questions.question: How can teams mitigate domain drift when using classifiers to filter web pages over months or years?
questions.choice_A: Schedule periodic refreshes of labeled data via active learning and hard-negative mining to retrain and recalibrate the model
questions.choice_B: Freeze the model and thresholds to maintain stable datasets across time
questions.choice_C: Only increase the embedding dimension to capture new terms without collecting labels
questions.choice_D: Switch to top-k selection only, because it is invariant to drift

questions.question: Which fastText loss configuration is commonly preferred for multilabel classification at scale?
questions.choice_A: CRF loss with sequence-level normalization
questions.choice_B: Hierarchical softmax with a Huffman tree per label and softmax outputs
questions.choice_C: One-vs-rest with independent sigmoid outputs (ova), optionally with negative sampling
questions.choice_D: Squared hinge loss over mutually exclusive classes

questions.question: Why is fastText a strong baseline for large-scale filtering compared to deeper architectures?
questions.choice_A: It always achieves higher final accuracy than transformers on any dataset.
questions.choice_B: It requires no hyperparameter tuning to perform well.
questions.choice_C: It learns universal semantic representations that do not need domain adaptation.
questions.choice_D: It offers competitive accuracy with very low training/inference cost, supports quantization, and scales linearly with data size

questions.question: What is a practical difference between thresholding and selecting top-k in retrieval pipelines?
questions.choice_A: Thresholding yields a variable number of items above a score cutoff; top-k returns a fixed number per query regardless of absolute scores
questions.choice_B: Thresholding requires calibrated probabilities; top-k cannot be applied to uncalibrated scores
questions.choice_C: Top-k selection is only valid for binary labels; thresholding is only for multilabel settings
questions.choice_D: Top-k is more robust to class imbalance than thresholding in all cases

questions.question: When aggregating top-k results across distributed shards at web scale, what is a key systems concern?
questions.choice_A: Ensuring each shard produces identical score distributions via shared random seeds
questions.choice_B: Merging per-shard heaps while maintaining global ranking and handling score calibration across shards
questions.choice_C: Discarding ties because they prevent reproducibility
questions.choice_D: Forcing each shard to return the same number of positives as negatives

questions.question: How can you calibrate classifier scores for better interpretability and stable thresholding across time?
questions.choice_A: Increase embedding dimension and number of epochs until validation loss stops improving
questions.choice_B: Switch from softmax to hierarchical softmax to reduce variance
questions.choice_C: Apply Platt scaling or isotonic regression on a held-out validation set to map scores to calibrated probabilities
questions.choice_D: Use a lower learning rate to reduce overconfidence

questions.question: What is a typical effect of increasing word n-gram length (e.g., wordNgrams from 1 to 2 or 3) in fastText classifiers?
questions.choice_A: It always improves generalization with no risk of overfitting or memory growth.
questions.choice_B: It reduces the need for hashing buckets because the feature space shrinks.
questions.choice_C: It eliminates the need for character n-grams to handle rare words.
questions.choice_D: It captures more phrases but expands the feature space, increasing memory/compute and potential overfitting without sufficient data

questions.question: Why might enabling character n-grams (minn/maxn) help in noisy or multilingual web data classification?
questions.choice_A: They provide subword evidence that improves robustness to misspellings, morphology, and out-of-vocabulary tokens
questions.choice_B: They force the model to ignore word boundaries, ensuring language-agnostic semantics
questions.choice_C: They allow the classifier to learn syntactic parse structures directly
questions.choice_D: They guarantee perfect cross-lingual transfer without additional labels

questions.question: How can weak supervision bootstrap training data for domain-relevant retrieval at scale?
questions.choice_A: By only labeling examples where multiple human annotators agree unanimously
questions.choice_B: By using heuristic rules (e.g., keyword/URL patterns) as noisy labels for seeds, then refining via validation and hard-negative mining
questions.choice_C: By replacing labels with unsupervised clustering outputs
questions.choice_D: By training on synthetic text generated by language models without any human verification

questions.question: Which inference strategy is most appropriate when latency is not critical but throughput is, for scoring billions of pages?
questions.choice_A: Per-request synchronous scoring with CPU pinning and small batches
questions.choice_B: GPU micro-batching to minimize latency spikes
questions.choice_C: On-device inference on web crawlers to decentralize scoring
questions.choice_D: Offline batch scoring with large batches, vectorized operations, and quantized models to maximize throughput

questions.question: In classifier-driven data collection, what practice helps avoid feedback loops and bias amplification?
questions.choice_A: Always setting very high thresholds so only the most confident pages are collected
questions.choice_B: Filtering out any examples that disagree with model predictions from the training set
questions.choice_C: Maintaining an exploration slice with diversity sampling and periodically injecting random or counterfactual examples for labeling
questions.choice_D: Training separate models per crawl without cross-validation to preserve independence
